title: FAA Lessons Learned from Civil Aviation Accidents as public accident-memory and pedagogy rail
summary: FAA Lessons Learned is encoded as a public aviation correction-memory rail: it turns selected accidents into modules, perspectives, threats, themes, and safety-practitioner teaching surfaces.

status_history.note: Added as rev0027 aviation human-factors/correction rail.

place.scope: aviation safety correction and human-factors infrastructure

subjects.name: FAA Lessons Learned from Civil Aviation Accidents

claims.claim: FAA describes its Lessons Learned library as information-rich modules drawn from selected large transport, small airplane, and rotorcraft accidents, with an objective of equipping current safety practitioners to apply lessons from past accidents.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: The FAA transport-airplane library page says it covers commercial passenger/cargo accidents worldwide, synthesizes safety-shaping accidents, lists a latest release of April 18, 2025, and records 97 modules.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: The FAA library organizes accident relationships through perspectives, elements, threat categories, and common themes, making it useful as a factor-translation rail for the cube.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

type_payload.signal_capture_model: officially selected accident modules synthesize investigation findings into pedagogical perspectives, threat categories, common themes, and design/operation lessons
outputs: links to accident records and recommendations
limitations: selection is not a complete denominator of aviation accidents
pedagogical modules are not substitutes for full official reports
existence of a lesson module does not prove correction infusion

handling_notes: Infrastructure records are correction-memory surfaces, not guarantees that recommendations or training actually changed practice.
Separate safety-investigation, training, public-lesson, legal, and regulatory rails.

unknowns: No denominator audit of all FAA module selection criteria was performed.
No recommendation-closure audit performed for cases in the library.
next_actions: Compare FAA Lessons Learned with NTSB CAROL and ASRS for memory/near-miss/recommendation distinction.
Add child records for specific module taxonomies once more aviation cases are promoted.
